original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first Federal Reserve H.15/FRED DGS10 observation explicitly dated 2026-08-18. Resolve the binary event TRUE if that first-published value is 4.70% or higher and FALSE if it is below 4.70%. Score probability with Brier and log loss. Score the point estimate by absolute error and record whether the 80% interval covers. Do not substitute later revisions unless the Federal Reserve corrects the initial release before scoring.
rationale: The Aug. 17 market 10-year quote was already near 4.724% and the 30-year yield reached its highest level since 2007, so a >=4.70% next-day constant-maturity reading is slightly more likely than not.

Renewed oil pressure plus Treasury/private-duration supply can keep long yields elevated even if softer activity lowers the expected policy path, directly testing the v0.2.4 state-dependent long-yield mechanism.
P000015 may reveal weak July industrial production on Aug. 18; such a result would normally pull yields lower, so the probability is only 0.58 rather than a high-confidence persistence call.
The absolute 4.70% threshold was fixed before the Aug. 18 industrial-production and housing releases and is close enough to the current yield to be meaningfully discriminating.
surprising_if: The 10-year rate falls below 4.60% despite continued oil pressure and no large positive duration-demand shock, indicating the growth/policy channel dominates the newly emphasized supply channel.
The 10-year rate rises above 4.85% after benign or weak activity data without a fresh inflation, fiscal, supply, or geopolitical catalyst.

resolution.source: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, observation dated 2026-08-18: 10-year CMT 4.71%. Treasury derives these CMTs from Federal Reserve Bank of New York indicative bid-side quotations near 3:30 PM. The contemporaneous FRED crawl had not yet refreshed, so the official Treasury table was used to verify the dated value corresponding to the H.15/FRED series.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved verbatim. The >=4.70% event resolved TRUE at 4.71%; the point forecast missed by 0.01 percentage point and the 80% interval covered. This single near-threshold success is evidence only for this forecast score and does not identify the private-duration mechanism or establish learning. Scored before post-cutoff evidence was used for model revision.
